validity.recommendation: Existence/classification are solid (real, under-construction gas branch line, correct developer). But verify/correct Diameter: GEM records a bare 250 (mm) while every independent source found describes this Laibin-branch trunk as 273.1mm OD pipe -- and this tracker's own convention elsewhere records that exact pipe class as '273.10' (two-decimal OD), not '250'. Recommend changing Diameter to 273.10mm unless a segment-specific spec sheet is found that truly supports 250 (nominal DN) as distinct from OD. Also spot-check Length (64.0km) and Capacity (0.30 bcm/y) against a primary segment-level document if one becomes reachable -- neither could be pinned to this exact sub-segment from sources we could reach.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: confirmed by two independent, verified, non-GEM sources that both name this exact segment. (1) Sina News (k.sina.com.cn), dated 2022-12-20: reports the groundbreaking ceremony for '广西燃气集团来宾天然气支线管道工程暨三江口新区天然气管道项目' at Liumian village, Chengxiang town, Xingbin District, on National Highway 314; developer Guangxi Gas Group Co Ltd; describes the Laibin branch route running Laibin distribution station -> Xingbin -> Wuxuan -> Xiangzhou -> Jinxiu Yao Autonomous County -> Jinxiu distribution station, with 3 new distribution stations, 1 refurbished station, 4 valve chambers; cites project-level pipe diameter 273.1mm, design pressure 4.0 MPa, design capacity 187 million m3/y (0.187 bcm/y), investment RMB 4.78 billion. (2) Laibin Daily (epaper.lbnews.com.cn), the city's official newspaper, dated 2023-08-09: public notice that the EIA report for '广西天然气支线管网项目来宾天然气支线管道工程（兴宾-武宣段）' -- i.e. this exact Xingbin-Wuxuan segment -- had been completed and was open for public comment, developer Guangxi Gas Group Co Ltd. Both sources match GEM's segment name, pipeline family, operator/owner and commodity exactly, so I'm confident this segment is real and correctly classified as a gas transmission branch line (not gathering/process line). The row's own cited ref (fgw.gxzf.gov.cn/.../t16217273.shtml) could not be verified -- it, and every other fgw.gxzf.gov.cn / dnr.gxzf.gov.cn URL surfaced during this audit, returned ConnectTimeout via url_verifier and ECONNREFUSED via WebFetch from this environment on repeated tries; Chinese provincial-government sites often geo-block requests from outside China, so this is inconclusive about the ref's validity, just unverifiable by us -- flagging for anyone with China-network access to re-check, not asserting the ref is dead. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate of any other roster PID -- no other of the 43 in-scope rows references Wuxuan, Xiangzhou or Jinxiu; a separate, related project on the same program ('Xingbin-Sanjiangkou segment', 43.7km, reached mechanical completion Nov 2025 per Sinopec contractor reporting) is a genuinely different route (toward Sanjiangkou New District, not Wuxuan) and is not represented in this 43-PID roster at all -- flagging as a side note only, out of scope for P7690 itself. SPEC: GEM Diameter=250mm (no decimal) is inconsistent with the 273.1mm OD figure both the Sina article and general reporting of the project-approval document (t13004479.shtml, unreachable to verify directly) give for this trunk; 273.1mm is also the standard Chinese OD for nominal DN250 pipe, and this same tracker records that exact pipe class elsewhere as '273.10' with two decimals -- strongly suggesting the P7690 row entered the DN (nominal) value into the OD-style Diameter field. Length: GEM's 64.0km for just the Xingbin-Wuxuan sub-segment is plausible against the ~148km aggregate figures reported for downstream/whole-route portions, but I could not independently source a document giving 64km (or any other number) specifically for the Xingbin-Wuxuan portion alone via a citable, verified URL, so treat with medium confidence rather than as confirmed. Capacity: GEM's 0.30 bcm/y (300 million m3/y) for this upstream sub-segment is arithmetically higher than the ~187 million m3/y (0.187 bcm/y) design-capacity figure the Sina piece gives for the branch overall, which is mildly inconsistent (an upstream segment's capacity is not usually less than the whole route's design figure) -- but that 187 figure itself came through an AI-summarized search result, not a document I verified directly, so I'm flagging rather than asserting either number wrong. Minor date-logic note: ProposalYear=2023 (Jan) postdates the Dec 2022 groundbreaking reported by Sina; plausible if 2023 reflects a later formal regulatory approval/批复 rather than the original public announcement, but worth a light check if anyone finds the original proposal announcement.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Searched for segment-specific news dated after the sheet's 2025-08-25 update, in Chinese, focused on '兴宾-武宣段' / '兴宾—武宣段'. Direct evidence for THIS exact segment tops out at 2023-08-09 (Laibin Daily EIA public-comment notice) -- no later news naming Xingbin-Wuxuan specifically was found (gxzf.gov.cn/dnr.gxzf.gov.cn government pages that likely hold the newest approvals are unreachable from this environment, ConnectTimeout/ECONNREFUSED on every attempt). However, a SIBLING segment on the same overall Laibin-branch program -- 'Xingbin-Sanjiangkou segment', a separate route, contractor Sinopec Henan Oil Construction -- only reached mechanical-completion inspection on 2025-11-13 (verified, entrepreneurdaily.cn), showing the broader multi-segment build-out is still actively under construction through late 2025, not dormant or abandoned. Given that pattern, 'construction' remains the most plausible current status for the Xingbin-Wuxuan segment specifically; I found no evidence of cancellation, shelving, or completion for it. Not treating as 'stale' because real, dated program activity (not zero) was found, just not segment-exact past 2023-08; dormancy rules for proposed/shelved statuses do not apply to a 'construction' row in any case.

summary: P7690 (Xingbin-Wuxuan segment) is a real, correctly classified gas branch line under Guangxi Gas Group -- confirmed via 2 independent Chinese sources (Sina groundbreaking article, Laibin Daily EIA notice) -- but its Diameter (250mm) looks like a DN-vs-OD mix-up against the sourced/tracker-convention 273.1mm, and Length/Capacity could not be independently pinned to the segment level; status=construction is corroborated as still-plausible via a sibling segment's Nov-2025 activity. No UNRESOLVED items.
